prompt:
Use case: one game icon for Under the Canopy, an RTS of insect armies on the forest floor, in the icon tradition of Warcraft III and StarCraft II. The game shows it at 46 pixels on its command card and as small as 22 pixels in buff badges: design it to read instantly at 32 pixels. Readability wins over every other wish.
THE RULES (every icon in the game follows them):
1. ONE subject showing ONE idea: exactly the object described below and nothing else. No second subject, no crowd of small figures, no scenery, no ground, no props around it.
2. A big, bold silhouette: the subject fills about 70% of the frame, centred a little up and left, and would be recognisable as a solid black shape alone. Chunky simple forms, crisp clean edges, no thin lines, no filigree, no small parts, no fine texture.
3. Light and value: one warm key light from the upper left. Paint the subject in three or four big value steps; its lit side is the brightest area of the whole icon. A thin bright rim light on the right edge separates it from the background.
4. Background: FULLY TRANSPARENT (real alpha) everywhere outside the subject and its own glow: no backdrop colour, gradient, texture, smoke, clouds, rays, sparkles, particles, bokeh, ground, cast shadow or vignette. A glow, where the icon has one, is semi-transparent and fades out completely well inside the frame. (The game puts its own background behind the icon.)
5. Limited palette: the subject's two or three main colours.
6. Effects (energy, lightning, fire, liquid, smoke, motion lines) ONLY where the subject below says the effect is part of it. Then the effect is one bold, simple shape (a single fork, a single splash, a single flame), never many thin strands or a glowing haze.
7. Rendering: hand-painted, stylised 3D like Warcraft III: Reforged icons, glossy materials with clear edge highlights, saturated but controlled colour.
8. Keep the bottom-right corner dark and empty (the game draws a hotkey letter there). NO text, letters, numbers, runes, symbols, UI, frame, border or bevel (the game adds the frame).
ICON TYPE: UNIT PORTRAIT. The unit's head and the top of its shoulders, like a Warcraft III unit icon: the head is LARGE, about half the frame's height, seen from the front-left three-quarter view, eyes in the upper third, cropped at the chest. Its one signature feature (horn, crest, mandibles, hood) is clearly visible; any weapon shows only as its tip at the edge, if at all. Behind the head, one soft warm amber glow (part of the icon, semi-transparent, fading out well inside the frame), bright enough that a dark chitin head reads sharply against it.
NEUTRAL FOREST CREATURES, the wild camps of the forest floor: chunky Warcraft proportions and a glossy finish, in their own natural materials (bark, moss, mushroom caps, water, fur, chitin, paper nests). Corrupted creatures show rot and magenta-violet spore light; none of them glows green.
REFERENCES: the first image is a small in-game render of this creature: keep its design, shapes and colours, but paint only its head and shoulders, larger, crisper and glossier; ignore its full-body pose.
THE SUBJECT: WILLOW WISP, a willow spirit: a round pale cream face with two big glossy black eyes, framed by a curtain of long drooping yellow-green willow leaves hanging down like hair, two small curved twig antlers and a few white blossoms on top, a small acorn amulet at its chest. Signature feature: the hanging willow-leaf curtain.
